events.title: Adele Goldberg co-releases Smalltalk-80
events.summary: Adele Goldberg and the Xerox PARC team released Smalltalk-80 in 1980 — pioneering GUIs, OOP, and live programming environments.
events.about: Smalltalk influenced Objective-C, Java, Ruby, and every IDE with a REPL or object browser. Goldberg famously showed Steve Jobs the Xerox GUI concepts that shaped the Macintosh.

narrative.whyChosen: Smalltalk-80 defined modern OOP and interactive development environments.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved objects and GUIs belonged together on personal computers.
narrative.problemSolved: Programming was batch-oriented without visual feedback or object metaphors.

events.title: Robert Metcalfe articulates network value scaling
events.quoteText: The value of a telecommunications network is proportional to the square of the number of connected users of the system.
events.summary: Ethernet inventor Robert Metcalfe articulated circa 1980 why network value grows with the square of users — later popularized as Metcalfe's Law by George Gilder in 1993.
events.about: Metcalfe's Law became the mental model behind social networks, marketplaces, and platform economics. Critics note n² oversimplifies real networks, but the core insight — connectivity has nonlinear returns — still shapes startup pitch decks.

narrative.whyChosen: The formula behind 'network effects' before the phrase existed.
narrative.whyImportant: It explained why winning platforms could pull away from rivals with similar features.
narrative.problemSolved: Investors and engineers lacked vocabulary for why connected products accelerate in value.
